Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-05 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SRE), Emma (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Lena Ortiz, Samir Khan, Priya Mehta, Alex Rivera (Orion)

Summary section auto-generated (may be rough): weekly POC sync - performance debrief - compared Redwood infra to Orion's current baseline with AcmeCloud. Discussed tuning steps and next run windows.

[00:00] Maya Singh: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: we want to walk through the benchmark numbers we ran this week, call out what changed since last sync, discuss some tail latency spikes samir saw, and confirm next runs. ok?
[00:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: yep that works. we got some internal complaints about slow responses around 3pm yesterday in our UI flow, so excited to see the numbers.
[00:28] Omar Patel: cool, i'll kick off with the high level. we ran the same workload mix you gave us — 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% med (64-256), 10% long (>256). baseline provider in your environment is AcmeCloud v1 endpoint, right?
[00:42] Samir Khan: yes, AcmeCloud managed endpoints, region us-west-2. we mirrored request patterns and replayed traces.
[00:50] Omar Patel: ok great. top-line: p50 latency on Redwood baseline config (hosted rw-v2-large quant-8) is 38ms for token generation (app-level p50 ~ 110ms), vs AcmeCloud p50 token time ~72ms (app p50 ~ 180ms). p95 on Redwood is ~120ms token (~340ms app), AcmeCloud p95 hit ~310ms token (~760ms app). throughput — in tokens/sec aggregate we saw 4200 tps on Redwood vs ~2900 tps on AcmeCloud under same concurrency.
[01:32] Priya Mehta: those numbers sound promising. can you explain what contributed most to the gaps? is it kernel optim, batching, or cache?
[01:40] Omar Patel: good q. it's a mix — kernel selection for attention + continuous batching improvements give per-token speed. also our KV/prefix cache hit rate was 74% in this run which saved a lot of compute for multiturn prompts. we turned on auto-batching (max batch 64) with latency SLO set to 180ms which allowed throughput gains without regressing tail too much.
[02:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: on the KV cache: our sessions are fairly long, will the cache hold across model variants and minor version rollouts?
[02:15] Jules Moreno: yes, cache keys are deterministically computed from session ids and model version is part of the key. when you pin a model version you maintain cache continuity; if we do a rollback we can map old keys to new variant only if compatible quant/profile — otherwise cache cold start occurs.
[02:34] Alex Rivera: we saw a couple of spikes last run where p95 jumped to 900ms for short prompts. what was the root cause?
[02:42] Omar Patel: we dug into that — two contributors: one was a network egress retry from a transient peering flake in your infra; second was a small GC stall on a node handling hot KV writes during a burst. we've patched an SRE mitigation that reduces KV write contention and Jules will coordinate a network test with you.
[03:02] Samir Khan: ok good. about quantization — you mentioned quant-8. we're exploring 4-bit too. any quality tradeoffs you've observed for our LLM family?
[03:12] Emma Zhao: yes, we ran quant-4 on a subset: latency improves further (~15% token speedup) and throughput increases ~20%, but on some narrow prompt families we saw small hallucination/formatting diffs. our recommendation: run an eval suite on your critical prompts; we can stage grade-level rollouts. Redwood Optimize can suggest per-route quant profiles to balance cost and QA.
[03:36] Priya Mehta: would that require code changes?
[03:39] Omar Patel: no code changes — it's routing/config at the inference layer. you can A/B route 10% to quant-4 and keep 90% quant-8 to watch metrics and regressions.
[03:48] Dr. Lena Ortiz: nice. about concurrency: we saw in our tests the baseline saturated at ~220 concurrent streams; you reported Redwood sustaining higher concurrency. what did your concurrency test look like?
[03:58] Omar Patel: we ran a 10-node parallel driver with controlled client concurrency ramp (up to 500 streams). Redwood stayed linear up to ~380 active streams before backpressure kicked in, baseline backpressured around 220. the difference was batching behavior and preemption policies — we employ small preemptive smoothing to keep tail latency stable.
[04:20] Maya Singh: i also want to call out cost delta — Emma has a cost sheet in the bench spreadsheet where you can see per-1M tokens cost for hosted vs dedicated. Dedicated shows better unit economics at scale but has commit requirements.
[04:31] Samir Khan: can you send that spreadsheet again? the link expired.
[04:34] Emma Zhao: yes will resend after call; i'll include the model config we used and the raw logs.
[04:38] [05:00] (Background: brief hold music while configuring screen share)
[05:12] Omar Patel: quick demo of the traces — here's a sample trace where prefix cache hit avoided 200ms extra compute on a 5-turn convo. (link: bench-spreadsheet/soak-08-04). note the KV hit column.
[05:34] Dr. Lena Ortiz: looks good. can you also annotate where network retries occurred so we can correlate with our infra logs?
[05:39] Jules Moreno: yes we'll add an egress-retry tag to the raw capture and push to the spreadsheet.
[05:45] Alex Rivera: about VPC peering — we want to run an iperf test and a controlled 2-hour window of production-like traffic to measure jitter/packet loss. what's your recommended window?
[05:55] Jules Moreno: weekdays 02:00–04:00 PST is low in your traffic profiles, but we can match whichever window you prefer. we'll need the IP ranges and a contact on your side for real-time monitoring.
[06:08] Priya Mehta: monday night works. alex will coordinate.
[06:12] Maya Singh: final section — risks and recommendations. Short version: Redwood shows meaningful latency and throughput gains vs AcmeCloud in our lab runs. main risks to watch: network peering flakiness, quantization regressions on edge prompts, and KV write contention under extreme bursts. mitigations: proposed 48h soak with mixed prompt sizes, targeted quant-4 A/B, and SRE-scheduled peering/iperf run.
[06:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sounds good. what's the proposed acceptance criteria to consider moving from pilot to dedicated?
[06:46] Maya Singh: we usually look at 3 things: sustained p95 below your target (you said 400ms app-level), throughput meeting your SLA (~3k tokens/sec), and a cost per 1M tokens within budget. if 48h soak meets those with no major regressions we can propose a Dedicated pilot quote.
[07:05] Samir Khan: ok agreed.
[07:08] Maya Singh: quick recap of next steps — Omar will run the 48h soak and share logs; Maya will send pricing appendix; Jules will schedule the VPC peering and do iperf; Emma will share spreadsheet + security pack. we'll reconvene next Friday same time unless you want earlier.
[07:28] Dr. Lena Ortiz: next Friday works. thanks everyone.
[07:32] Maya Singh: thanks — closing notes: links we'll send after call: bench spreadsheet, pricing appendix, SOC2 / KMS notes, tuned config snippet.
[07:42] (Meeting ends)
